_doc: REGISTER OF ACCEPTED DIVERGENCES from Claude Code — the things this port
deliberately does differently, and the guards that only LOOK like removable
redundancy. A parity audit must triage anything listed here as settled, not
re-find it as a gap.
Why it is a file and not a note: this list lived outside the repository, in a
Claude memory, while code and tests referenced it. CI could not read it, a
fresh clone could not read it, and nothing could tell whether an entry was
still true. Migrating it on 2026-09-10 immediately found two that were not:
the plugin function-hook runtime, recorded as 'absent and not new', had since
been built (AG-15); and 'crossreview', recorded as a LingXi-exclusive feature,
has zero production hits and survives only in old design docs. Both are kept
below as `retired` rather than deleted, because a divergence that quietly
disappears is indistinguishable from one nobody has checked.
Shape borrowed from `workflow/src/workflow_description_divergences.json`,
which replaced a bare byte-count with an anchored register for the same
reason: a count cannot tell 'deliberate' from 'drifted'.
Each active entry carries at least one anchor, checked by
`tests/parity_accepted_divergences.rs`:
* `present` — the text must still appear at `path`. This is the anchor for
'we do it our own way': it fails when the thing we point at is renamed or
deleted, i.e. when the entry stops describing the code.
* `absent`  — the text must have zero hits under `path`. This is the anchor
for 'we deliberately do not have this', and it is the half that would have
caught the function-hook entry the day it went stale.
`decided_by: "user"` means a human made the call on that date and it is not
the auditor's to revisit; `decided_by: "oracle"` means the binary itself
settles it (a default-false gate, a stale mirror) and new oracle evidence can.

divergences.finding: Claude Code speaks only to Anthropic's API.
divergences.reason: LingXi is a multi-provider product by design (OpenAI, GLM, Bedrock, Vertex, OpenAI Responses/WebSocket, plus provider catalog and routing). Any code path that branches on model identity must therefore have defined behaviour for an id it does not recognise — that is the normal case here, not an edge.

divergences.finding: Claude Code ships its own web search stack.
divergences.reason: LingXi implements WebSearch itself (Tavily-backed). Do not port Claude's stack over it.

divergences.finding: Claude Code has no mobile host.
divergences.reason: LingXi ships Android and iOS surfaces. They are additions, not gaps, and a parity sweep must not try to reconcile them against a CLI that has no equivalent.

divergences.finding: Claude Code uses CLAUDE_* env vars, ~/.claude and CLAUDE.md.
divergences.reason: LingXi uses its own namespace throughout. Env-var kill switches should accept both spellings where parity-relevant, but the canonical names are LingXi's.

divergences.finding: The Workflow tool description enumerates five EXHAUSTIVE opt-in clauses and closes with 'For any other task ... do NOT call this tool.'
divergences.reason: None of the five covers the local-app create flow, where the MODEL self-invokes the create skill and that skill specifies the Workflow call. Without a sixth clause every create is a call the model has been told not to make. The edit itself is registered byte-for-byte next door.

divergences.finding: Claude Code auto-expires recurring jobs seven days after creation (`recurringMaxAgeMs`), and says so in the CronCreate result, schema and prompt.
divergences.reason: LingXi has no global age limit: expiry is per task via `expiresAt`, and absent means never. The CronCreate prompt's seven-day paragraph is gated on the port's own `default_recurring_max_age()`, so it stays byte-exact to the oracle exactly where the behaviour exists. The dynamic /loop aged-out guard is a separate mechanism and stays oracle-faithful.

divergences.finding: 2.1.266 has a `ProposeGoal` tool and a cloud 'ultraplan' remote plan mode.
divergences.reason: ProposeGoal is dormant twice over upstream: its flag defaults false and its isEnabled also bails on non-interactive or remote, which is this engine's shape. It also needs an interactive dialog and a message-queue enqueue there is no seat for. Ultraplan is plan mode running in Claude Code on the web, with cloud session URLs and PR delivery — no substrate here. The name still appears in the ported upstream tool-name tables; what is absent is any implementation.

divergences.finding: 2.1.267 adds a subagent hand-back contract: a child delivers its report through a dedicated tool, with an enforcement path and a send/flagged/withheld disposition.
divergences.reason: Gated on `tengu_lively_waffle`, which defaults FALSE, plus auto-mode. On a host with no statsig backend — this port — a default install of 2.1.267 behaves exactly as LingXi does, so the absence IS the alignment. Building it now would port a mechanism upstream does not run. Revisit if the gate flips or the env override appears in a real environment.

divergences.finding: Upstream carries two turn-interrupt strings alongside `[Request interrupted by user]`: one for a tool call that had started when the turn was ended to deliver a message, one for a call that had not run.
divergences.reason: They describe a mechanism this port deliberately does not have — ending a turn MID-TOOL-CALL to deliver an inbound message. Here a message queues, the agent parks, and the queue drains as a digest at rest. Porting the strings would produce markers nothing can emit. Reopen only alongside an interrupting-delivery path; both are needed then, and the distinction between them matters.

That mirror is stale: both are zero hits in the 2.1.267 and 2.1.263 binaries, and skill names survive minification as string literals, so a zero there is decisive. `stuck` is not one either — it has many hits as the English word and no registration. The bundled set must be read off registrations, never off a substring count.

divergences.finding: 2.1.267 introduces plugin surface modules and a JSX render runtime (`$.ui.resolve`, `ClientElements`, `exportTree`, the Box/Text/Button/Client/Svg element set).
divergences.reason: New in 267 and unbuilt here. It shares the JS-worker seam with the rest of the plugin runtime — scope it as its own project or not at all, never as an audit finding.

divergences.finding: 2.1.223 ships a `claude-code-guide` builtin agent and a `claude` catch-all.
divergences.reason: Both steer the user toward Claude-specific documentation and products, which is wrong in a multi-provider product. Removed deliberately; do not resurrect either for byte parity. The reverse correction also stands: the agent model enum's `fable` value IS native upstream and is parity, not a divergence.

divergences.finding: The `claudeai-proxy` transport and the claude.ai connector surface are out of scope, but two PARSER-fidelity gaps were explicitly authorized for fixing.
divergences.reason: `request_timeout_ms` was being folded into `timeout` where the oracle declares neither the field nor a transform, and `id` is REQUIRED for this transport and was neither modelled nor validated. Do NOT revert these as anti-parity, and do NOT generalize the carve-out: the deliberate fold onto the Http transport and the whole connector feature surface remain out of scope. 'Make the parser honest about a shape we already accept' is the boundary.

divergences.finding: `/cost` and `/stats` have no independent content — they are aliases of `/usage`.
divergences.reason: This LOOKS like removable redundancy and is not: Claude Code itself defines the usage command with those two aliases, so deleting them would be the divergence. The real recorded gap is `/usage` CONTENT missing upstream rows, which is data-plumbing-gated. Fix direction is to fill `/usage`, never to remove `/cost`.

divergences.finding: `functionHooks` / `hooks-worker` — the JS-worker hook runtime, present in 2.1.245 through 2.1.267 alike.
divergences.reason: Recorded as a long-standing absence rather than a 2.1.267 delta, on the grounds that the whole JS-worker hook runtime was zero hits here and `HookEvent` carried only the command hooks.
divergences.retired_because: Overtaken the same day: the AG-15 series built it. `hooks/src/function_hook.rs` exists, `HookEvent` carries the function-hook path, and a plugin can declare one. The entry is kept rather than deleted because it is the case that proves why this register has `absent` anchors — it was true when written and false a few commits later, and nothing outside a person's memory would have noticed.

divergences.finding: Recorded as a LingXi-exclusive feature alongside the mobile surfaces.
divergences.reason: Listed among the additions a parity sweep must not try to reconcile against Claude Code.
divergences.retired_because: Zero hits in production code at migration time; it survives only in `docs/multi-agent-*.md` design notes. Either it was never built or it was removed, and an entry defending a feature that does not exist protects nothing while making the list look longer than it is.
